chapters.title: Chapter 1 - One Suitcase
chapters.summary: Hollywood, 1935. One suitcase, a few dollars, a room at Bellhaven and a lead at Sunset Casting. By the end of the chapter the Boulevard knows your name.

arcs.title: Getting Noticed
arcs.summary: From a first audition at the casting office to a screen test, earning the gatekeeper's trust along the way.

beats.title: Book a first audition
beats.summary: Talk your way past the clerk at Sunset Casting Exchange and get on the books.

beats.title: Land the screen test
beats.summary: A callback, some experience and the gatekeeper's trust open the door to a screen test.

arcs.title: A Place to Land
arcs.summary: Making rent at Bellhaven and finding friends at the diner: the everyday life behind the ambition.

beats.title: Make rent at Bellhaven
beats.summary: Settle up with the landlady and earn your keep.

beats.title: Introduce yourself at the diner
beats.summary: Win over the counter crowd at The Gilded Spoon and earn a confidant.

arcs.title: The Rival at the Gate
arcs.summary: A rival with her own hard-won ambitions, met at the Monarch Pictures gate.

beats.title: Cross paths at the Monarch gate
beats.summary: First encounter with the rival; standing your ground earns respect.

arcs.title: On the Lot
arcs.summary: Getting work, rehearsing and being seen: extras calls, scene work, wardrobe, press and the Palace.

beats.title: Answer an extras call
beats.summary: Check in with the production coordinator and get cleared for call.

beats.title: Rehearse with a scene partner
beats.summary: Run the scene together and find the rhythm.

beats.title: Get fitted for the part
beats.summary: The wardrobe mistress at The Silver Thimble sizes you up.

beats.title: Give the newsman something
beats.summary: Feed The Klieg Light a story and see it in print.

beats.title: A matinee at The Celestial Palace
beats.summary: Earn the house manager's offer of a matinee seat and attend.

arcs.title: Chapter 1 Conclusion
arcs.summary: All ten quests done: the Conclusion card recaps the chapter and hands off to Chapter 2.

beats.title: The Conclusion screen
beats.summary: A green-bordered title card with a story recap, then back to the Boulevard with "Chapter 2 - Coming Soon" in the quest helper.

chapters.carryForward: The ten Chapter 1 quests establish the cast and the places. Every origin starting contact is met. The Conclusion card hands off to Chapter 2.

chapters.title: Chapter 2 - A Small Part
chapters.summary: The screen test lands the player a small speaking part in The Corsair's Daughter, their first real credit. On set they meet the leading man, glimpse the man who owns the studio, and have to decide whom their heart is pointing toward.
chapters.carryForward: First credit earned (the Lookout), which opens Selma Pruitt's and Ray Kessler's doors wider and sets a first reputation band. The love interest is chosen and stays the anchor of the player's romance track (or a close friendship if the player prefers). Hollis Pike and Maddox are seeded as background, and Gus's invitation opens the Bowl. Attributes: the set day leans on Craft, Wit and Nerve; XP roughly 100 for the chapter, enough to reach level 4. New assignments keep unlocking by level.

arcs.title: Cast
arcs.summary: From screen test result to first day on the soundstage.

beats.title: The test lands
beats.summary: Selma Pruitt and Ray Kessler deliver the verdict on the screen test: a small speaking part in The Corsair's Daughter, the Lookout, a harbor-market pickpocket with three lines who warns the heroine. A strong test earns a fourth line and a better call time; a partial one still gets the part.
beats.choices: Accept the part as offered, or push for one more line (Presence or Wit check).
beats.routes: Wit + Comedy, or Presence + Charm to negotiate; Craft + Drama to have earned it outright.
beats.effects: First credit. Reputation up a band. Ray's trust begins.

beats.title: Fitted for the harbor market
beats.summary: Ola Whitfield fits the Lookout's costume at The Silver Thimble and quietly teaches the player how a garment photographs. Studio-Lot Hand-Me-Down players get the wardrobe shortcut.
beats.choices: How the player wears the costume: bold, practical or borrowed.
beats.routes: Craft + Stagecraft for camera-ready detail.
beats.effects: Costume item for the home display. Ola's trust.
beats.notes: Built without the Studio-Lot Hand-Me-Down shortcut: dialogue has no origin condition yet, so every origin gets the same fitting. Camera-ready detail is gated on Stagecraft I.

beats.title: First day on the set
beats.summary: The big day on the soundstage: Ray runs the call, Corinne Lake and Theo Marchetti are filming the harbor-market chase, and the player has one scene. A flubbed line, a stuck prop and a nervous director turn it into a small Read the Room: hit the mark, read the cue, recover.
beats.choices: Stay in the script, improvise around the flub, or take the blame for the stuck prop.
beats.routes: Craft + Drama (clean take); Wit + Comedy (improvise); Nerve + Stagecraft (hold the scene together).
beats.effects: XP and reputation by take quality. Corinne and Theo meet the player. Pike takes the publicity stills and notes the newcomer.
beats.notes: The set day is a Read the Room scene (lookout-first-day) with five categories; the three choices in the draft are its improvisation and adaptation options.

arcs.title: The Heart's Choice
arcs.summary: A week of small scenes with four people, then a dance.

beats.title: A week of rehearsals
beats.summary: Between shoots the player spends time with the four people the story lets them choose between: Corinne Lake at the soundstage, Frankie Dolan at the diner counter, Delphine Voss at the gate, and Theo Marchetti on set. Each has a short warm scene and one awkward one. Nothing is committed yet.
beats.choices: Who to spend each free evening with; how candid to be.
beats.routes: Charm + Presence for charisma scenes; Wit for banter; Grit for the long-hours bond with Theo.
beats.effects: Attraction and trust meters set for all four. Nobody is locked out until the dance.

beats.title: Wrap party at The Celestial Palace
beats.summary: Lucian Vale opens the Palace ballroom for the company's wrap party. There is one dance to give. The player chooses a love interest (or chooses to keep everyone as friends). Longing looks and a dance only: no kiss.
beats.choices: Corinne Lake, Frankie Dolan, Delphine Voss, Theo Marchetti, or no one yet.
beats.routes: Any build can be charming; a low Presence costs the dance an extra nervous beat.
beats.effects: The love interest is chosen and recorded. Friends-only is a full, equally rewarded path.
beats.notes: Built without the extra nervous beat for low Presence: dialogue has no attribute condition yet. Nobody is locked out of any dance.

arcs.title: Whispers
arcs.summary: Rivalry and the first hint of who runs the town.

beats.title: Delphine's warning
beats.summary: Delphine Voss corners the player outside the gate: she is not sorry to see a rival, and she is not sure she is one. Depending on earlier choices she sabotages, tests or offers an alliance.
beats.choices: Stand your ground, match her edge, or offer a truce.
beats.routes: Nerve + Charm; Wit to read what she really wants.
beats.effects: Sets Delphine's arc (friend, rival, romance or enemy) for the rest of the story.

beats.title: The helpful man
beats.summary: Hollis Pike introduces himself with a business card and an offer to "look after" the player's image, and Leopold Maddox is seen once through the office window above the soundstage. Nick Ferro offers a trade for an exclusive. Every favor is small, and the player notices none of them is free.
beats.choices: Accept Pike's help, refuse politely, or bargain with Nick instead.
beats.routes: Wit + Observation to spot the hooks; Hustle to use them.
beats.effects: Accepting starts the ledger: each accepted favor is tracked and matters in Chapters 7 to 10. Declining costs nothing now.

beats.title: An invitation under the stars
beats.summary: Gus Albrecht, with a rare twinkle, invites the player to the Hollywood Bowl: a friend's tickets, a summer evening and "someone I want you to see". Bellhaven will lend an evening outfit.
beats.choices: Go, or go later.
beats.effects: Opens the Hollywood Bowl. First assignment-style task to earn the evening money.
beats.notes: The evening money is a $10 chip-in at Bellhaven or a favor owed to the landlady, not a new assignment (assignment balance is unchanged).

chapters.title: Chapter 3 - Under the Stars
chapters.summary: A summer concert at the Hollywood Bowl with Gus, and a chance encounter with a director who notices people other than the stars.
chapters.carryForward: The Bowl opens as a new location and the map stays open: the Boulevard can be revisited for side scenes and small XP, but Gus now lives at the Bowl. The chance encounter sets Anton Reiss's regard, which drives the next chapter. Attributes: Wit and Observation carry the encounter. Reputation gains come from how the player carries themselves in public.

arcs.title: A Night Out with Gus
arcs.summary: The evening that gives Gus his story and the player their start.

beats.title: Getting there
beats.summary: The hills above Hollywood: the player travels to the Bowl for the first time, Ola or Bellhaven supplies evening clothes, and the player earns the last of the ticket money. The map opens.
beats.choices: Borrow the clothes, tailor them, or earn the money for a new collar.
beats.routes: Hustle for the money; Craft or Stagecraft for the fitting.
beats.effects: Hollywood Bowl unlocked. Gus leaves the extras corral and is now found at the Bowl.

beats.title: The picnic box
beats.summary: Before the music, on the terrace, Gus tells the player how close he once came: a vaudeville bill, a screen test in 1921, a lost chance. A warm, funny, honest scene that deepens the mentor bond.
beats.choices: Listen, joke, or push him to tell the whole story.
beats.routes: Charm + Observation to draw it out; Grit to stay patient.
beats.effects: Gus's trust. Unlocks Gus's signature advice (a one-time audition bonus in Chapter 4).

beats.title: Symphony under the stars
beats.summary: Maestro Felix Arnaud conducts. In the VIP boxes: Coralie Dane on Leopold Maddox's arm, Hollis Pike two rows behind, and Delphine Voss in the cheap seats, looking up. The player sees the whole ladder of Hollywood in one amphitheater.
beats.choices: Who to greet, who to ignore.
beats.effects: Coralie Dane is introduced as the next rival. Maddox notices the player in passing.

arcs.title: A Chance Encounter
arcs.summary: The VIP director in the next box.

beats.title: The dropped score
beats.summary: At the interval an elderly man in the neighboring box is trying to read a score he has dropped in the dark. The player has a moment and a choice about how to meet him, not knowing who he is.
beats.choices: Help quietly, help with a joke, or hand back the score with a sharp observation about the conductor.
beats.routes: Charm (gracious), Wit + Comedy (light), Observation + Nerve (bold).
beats.effects: Sets Reiss's first impression; each route is valid.

beats.title: Who is Anton Reiss?
beats.summary: Gus recognises him. Billie Okafor arrives, apologising for her employer, and Reiss tests the stranger with a question: what did you notice about the cellists? The answer is the audition before the audition.
beats.choices: What to say about what you saw.
beats.routes: Observation + Wit gives the sharpest answer; Drama + Presence gives the most moving one; Hustle + Charm works the room.
beats.effects: Reiss's regard is set: high if the answer is honest and specific, modest if flashy.

beats.title: The invitation
beats.summary: After the last encore Reiss says that he is casting The Lantern Keeper, a quiet sea-drama, and that he will see the player in two weeks. Hollis Pike appears within seconds, smiling, to note the name. Maddox's shadow is on it already.
beats.choices: Accept on his terms, or ask for the script first.
beats.effects: The audition is scheduled. Pike reports the conversation to Maddox.

chapters.title: Chapter 4 - The Audition
chapters.summary: Two weeks to prepare for the audition of a lifetime, a rival who wants the same part, and a verdict that is interrupted by the man who owns the studio.

targets.housing: Boarding-house room, apartment affordable by the end

chapters.carryForward: The full Read the Room system is the test of the chapter. The first signature talent unlocks at level 5: "The Quiet Room" (Craft). An apartment ($150) becomes affordable by the end of the chapter. Reiss's regard and the player's callback carry into Chapters 5 and 6 as the thing the publicity is for.

arcs.title: Preparing
arcs.summary: Study, commit, rehearse.

beats.title: Study
beats.summary: Billie Okafor gives the player ten pages of The Lantern Keeper: the storm scene where Wren, the Keeper's ward, must keep the light burning alone. The Study phase of Read the Room: read, ask, notice.
beats.choices: What to ask Billie; which pages to dwell on.
beats.routes: Observation + Craft to find what the scene is really about; Charm to earn Billie's hints.
beats.effects: Each thing learned is a preparation check in the audition.

beats.title: Rehearsal under the shell
beats.summary: Early mornings in the empty Bowl: the player rehearses with whoever they chose as love interest, a friend, or Gus. Acoustics, echo and the open sky teach projection and restraint.
beats.choices: Who to rehearse with, and whether to work on voice, stillness or movement.
beats.routes: Drama + Stagecraft for the stage presence route; Comedy to loosen the scene; Dance for movement.
beats.effects: Raises the player's preparation and the rehearsal partner's trust or attraction.

beats.title: The golden girl wants it too
beats.summary: Coralie Dane drops by, charming and brittle, to size up the competition. Hollis Pike is three steps behind her. Delphine Voss, unseen, leaves the player a warning note. Coralie is not cruel; she is cornered.
beats.choices: Befriend Coralie, compete openly, or ignore her.
beats.routes: Charm + Wit to reach her; Nerve to stay steady.
beats.effects: Seeds Coralie as a person, not just an obstacle. Friendly choices give the player her trust at the Pier and the gala.

arcs.title: The Test
arcs.summary: The audition itself, and what comes after.

beats.title: The read
beats.summary: The major audition, held in a rehearsal hall beneath the band shell with Reiss and Billie watching. A full Read the Room: commit, perform, then adapt when Reiss changes the scene mid-take.
beats.choices: Intention and technique; delivery; one improvised change when Reiss interrupts.
beats.routes: Drama + Craft (truthful), Comedy + Wit (surprising), Dance + Stagecraft (physical), Charm + Presence (magnetic). Any build can carry the scene; the debrief shows the contributing factors.
beats.effects: Success: a callback with real interest. Partial: a callback with conditions. Fail-forward: an offer to read in a workshop. Never a dead end.

beats.title: The verdict
beats.summary: Reiss does not say yes. He says that the picture does not exist yet, and that he wants the player in it. Then Hollis Pike arrives with a message: Mr. Maddox will "review the slate" before any casting is final.
beats.choices: Press Reiss for a commitment, stay gracious, or confront Pike.
beats.routes: Nerve + Presence to press; Charm to stay gracious.
beats.effects: Reiss's regard recorded. The project is now at Maddox's mercy.

beats.title: A telegram from Nick
beats.summary: The project needs momentum it does not have. A telegram from Nick Ferro: "Pier. Saturday. Bring your best smile and someone worth photographing." The Pier opens.
beats.choices: Go, and with whom.
beats.effects: Santa Monica Pier unlocked. Gus remains at the Bowl.

chapters.title: Chapter 5 - Salt and Flashbulbs
chapters.summary: A day on the pier, arranged by Nick Ferro, to give the stalled project some headlines, with a rival who is also there for the cameras.
chapters.carryForward: Publicity is the new currency: every pier beat adds to or drains the reputation bar, and scandal risk is introduced. The apartment is taken (Chapter 4 money). Level 6 adds the dance and hustle routes at the pier games.

arcs.title: Making Headlines
arcs.summary: A publicity day on the pier.

beats.title: A day at the pier
beats.summary: Nick Ferro has set up a photo layout: "The Boulevard's Brightest Hope". The carousel, the arcade, the boardwalk and the dance pavilion are the settings, and the player chooses how to pitch themselves.
beats.choices: Funny, dashing, earnest or mysterious: each pitch changes the caption.
beats.routes: Comedy + Charm (funny), Presence + Dance (dashing), Drama (earnest), Nerve + Hustle (mysterious).
beats.effects: Sets the public image. The image matters in every later scene at a gala or a premiere.

beats.title: Dizzy's camera
beats.summary: Dizzy Quinn takes the picture that will run. Pier games along the way: a dance-off at the pavilion, a ring toss, a fortune teller who is uncomfortably accurate. Each is a small contextual showdown.
beats.choices: Which games to play and how much to show off.
beats.routes: Dance + Hustle for the dance-off; Observation for the booth; Nerve for the wheel.
beats.effects: Small money, XP and a gallery of pier photographs for the home display.

beats.title: Lavinia Crowe's column
beats.summary: The Evening Beacon's Lavinia Crowe is on the pier for the crowd. She will print whatever she is given, and she is not above inventing. The player can feed her, flatter her or freeze her out, each with consequences.
beats.choices: Feed, flatter or refuse.
beats.routes: Wit + Charm to spin; Nerve to refuse; Hustle to trade.
beats.effects: Reputation risk: a refused Lavinia may print the worst version. Handled by implication only.

arcs.title: The Golden Girl
arcs.summary: Coralie and Delphine on the boardwalk.

beats.title: Coralie on the boardwalk
beats.summary: Coralie Dane arrives with Hollis Pike for a "spontaneous" studio shoot. The two careers collide in front of Dizzy's camera, and the player decides whether to upstage, befriend or simply be kind.
beats.choices: Upstage her, share the frame, or step back.
beats.routes: Presence + Charm to share; Nerve + Wit to upstage.
beats.effects: Coralie's trust or tension. If the player was kind in Chapter 4 she slips the player a warning.

beats.title: Delphine at the carousel
beats.summary: Delphine Voss has come on her own, without her usual armor. Depending on earlier choices, she offers a real truce, a last warning, or a confession about what Maddox asked of her.
beats.choices: Accept the truce, stay wary, or tell her what you know.
beats.routes: Wit + Observation to read what she is hiding.
beats.effects: Delphine's arc advances toward ally, friend, romance or enemy.

beats.title: The sun starts to go down
beats.summary: The afternoon ends. The love interest (or the friend the player invited) arrives for the walk along the pier at sunset. The flashbulbs are packed away. Chapter 6 begins.
beats.effects: Transition beat into the sunset scene.

chapters.title: Chapter 6 - Sunset on the Pier
chapters.summary: A sunset on the Ferris wheel with the person the player chose, a whisper of inside information about what Maddox is planning, and a morning of headlines.
chapters.carryForward: The romantic scene and the inside information are the heart of the chapter; the information gives the player the knowledge that the later chapters turn on. Publicity raises reputation sharply and opens the Observatory invitation. The second signature talent, "Headliner" (Presence), unlocks. The love interest is now either a romance (a kiss at high trust) or a close friend, equally rewarded.

arcs.title: The Sunset
arcs.summary: The romantic encounter and what it reveals.

beats.title: The long walk
beats.summary: Down the length of the pier as the light turns gold. The chosen love interest (Corinne Lake, Frankie Dolan, Delphine Voss or Theo Marchetti) and the player talk about what they want, what they are afraid of, and what the town is doing to them both. A dialogue scene whose tone follows the relationship built so far.
beats.choices: How honest to be; what to ask; what to give.
beats.routes: Charm + Wit for warm banter; Drama for the vulnerable beat; Grit for the shared-hardship beat.
beats.effects: Attraction and trust step up. A friends-only player has the same scene written as a close friendship.

beats.title: At the top of the wheel
beats.summary: The Ferris wheel stops at the top, and the whole bay is gold. Longing looks, a held hand, a spoken feeling, and at high trust one tasteful kiss that cuts away to the sunset. The mood breaks gently when the love interest, trusting the player, says what they know.
beats.choices: Say it back, say less, or change the subject.
beats.routes: Presence (command the moment), Charm, Nerve (lean in).
beats.effects: Romance deepens or becomes a settled friendship. The inside information is delivered in the love interest's own voice.
beats.notes: Romance ceiling: longing looks, hand-holding, one tasteful kiss that cuts away, spoken declarations. No innuendo.

beats.title: What they told you
beats.summary: The inside information, from the person the player trusts: Leopold Maddox intends to buy out The Lantern Keeper and cast Coralie Dane unless the picture gets public momentum by month's end; and Hollis Pike keeps a ledger of the studio's favors and payments. Each love interest knows a different piece, so the full picture needs the others later.
beats.choices: Keep the secret, share it with Nick Ferro, or take it to Reiss.
beats.routes: Wit + Observation to see what it means.
beats.effects: The player now holds two pieces of knowledge that shape the endings: the buyout and the ledger.

beats.title: Flashbulbs
beats.summary: Dizzy Quinn's lens and Nick Ferro's notebook both caught the wheel, the light and the two figures at the top. The morning edition runs a photograph and a line: "Who is the Boulevard's Mystery Sweetheart?"
beats.choices: Own the photograph, deny it, or turn it into a joke.
beats.routes: Comedy + Charm to own it; Nerve + Hustle to handle the fallout.
beats.effects: Big publicity spike. Reputation jumps a band. The scandal gauge rises if Lavinia Crowe is unhandled.

arcs.title: The Morning Edition
arcs.summary: What the town said next.

beats.title: Two columns
beats.summary: Nick's warm piece and Lavinia's sly one run side by side. The public picks; so does Hollywood. A response in the right tone turns the story to the player's favor.
beats.choices: Answer Lavinia, let Nick answer for you, or say nothing.
beats.routes: Wit + Charm; Nerve to ignore.
beats.effects: Reputation fork.

beats.title: Reiss sends Billie
beats.summary: The momentum is real. Billie Okafor arrives at Bellhaven (or wherever the player lives now) with a hand-written note from Reiss: the picture lives, and an invitation to Monarch's gala at the Griffith Observatory. The buyout is postponed, not cancelled.
beats.choices: Go to the gala, and with whom.
beats.effects: Griffith Observatory unlocked. "Headliner" signature talent unlocked.

chapters.title: Chapter 7 - Stars Over Hollywood
chapters.summary: Monarch's midnight gala at the new Observatory. The player meets Leopold Maddox, is offered a small favor, is approached in secret by Coralie Dane, and at midnight, as the planetarium lights go down, Coralie is found dead.
chapters.timeframe: Early October 1935, the night of the gala
chapters.carryForward: The ledger begins to bite: any favors the player accepted from Pike or Maddox are now owed. The player's earlier kindness or rivalry with Coralie and Delphine decides who trusts them. Evidence, the new currency of the next chapter, starts here. The bungalow ($500) is affordable. Tone guardrail: a cozy, bloodless mystery; nothing graphic.

arcs.title: The Gala
arcs.summary: Glamour, a favor and a secret.

beats.title: Arrival on the hill
beats.summary: The Observatory at dusk: the dome, the terrace, the whole city below. Everyone is here: Maddox, Pike, Reiss, Billie, Nick, Lavinia, Delphine, Corinne and Theo. The player arrives with the love interest or a friend and sees the building they will have to read tonight.
beats.choices: Whom to greet first; how to dress the part.
beats.routes: Presence + Charm to work the room.
beats.effects: Sets the night's social graph. Dr. Whitcombe gives an unhurried tour of the Hall of Science, the pendulum and the planetarium.

beats.title: Leopold Maddox
beats.summary: The mogul finally meets the player, gentle and exact. He praises the Pier pictures, says Reiss is a great man to be admired from a distance, and offers a small favor: a word in the right column, a better dressing room. "No obligation." Every word of it is a loan.
beats.choices: Accept the favor, decline, or ask what it costs.
beats.routes: Wit + Observation to read him; Nerve to decline; Hustle to bargain.
beats.effects: Accepting adds a ledger entry and the player's name to Pike's book. Declining earns Maddox's quiet respect and his attention.

beats.title: Coralie in the dome corridor
beats.summary: Coralie Dane finds the player alone: frightened, in whispers. She has read part of the ledger, she is going to Nick Ferro in the morning, and she does not know who to trust. "Meet me after the show." A player who was kind in Chapters 4 and 5 is told more.
beats.choices: Promise to meet her, offer to go with her now, or warn her off.
beats.routes: Observation + Nerve to sense the danger; Charm to earn the trust.
beats.effects: Sets how much Coralie confides. Every route leaves the player with a reason to care who did it.

arcs.title: Midnight
arcs.summary: The lights go down.

beats.title: The planetarium show
beats.summary: At midnight Dr. Whitcombe dims the dome for "Stars Over Hollywood". Two minutes of darkness, the stars turning, and a soft sound somewhere behind the pendulum. When the lights come up, everyone is exactly where they were, except one.
beats.choices: Where the player sits and what they watch.
beats.routes: Observation (what moved), Nerve (stay calm), Grit (stay put).
beats.effects: What the player watched during the dark becomes their first clues.

beats.title: The Hall of Science
beats.summary: Coralie Dane is found in the Hall of Science, beside the pendulum: a champagne cordial glass beside her, no mark on her, every clue implied rather than shown. Lieutenant Finch arrives and closes the building until dawn.
beats.choices: Stay with the body, stay with the love interest, or slip to the dome.
beats.effects: Tone: cozy, bloodless, implied. The mystery begins.
beats.notes: Guardrail: no gore, no graphic depiction; the cause is discovered, never shown.

beats.title: Suspects in the dome
beats.summary: Finch asks everyone to wait in the planetarium. The suspects: Delphine Voss (lost the role to Coralie), Nick Ferro (the source of her story), Hollis Pike (her handler), Theo Marchetti, Corinne Lake and Dr. Whitcombe. The player has until dawn, and Lieutenant Finch is quietly counting on them.
beats.choices: Whom to defend, whom to press, whom to trust.
beats.routes: Charm + Presence for statements; Observation + Wit for cross-checking.
beats.effects: Sets each suspect's starting suspicion score.

chapters.title: Chapter 8 - Midnight at the Observatory
chapters.summary: One night to find out who killed the player's biggest rival. The clues fit different people depending on what the player noticed, and the solution is under the planetarium stars.
chapters.carryForward: Evidence collected carries into the ending: the ledger pages and Pike's confession are what makes the exposure possible in Chapter 10. The player's handling of Delphine and Nick decides whether they are allies later. "Sharp Eyes" (Wit) unlocks as the third signature talent. A wrong accusation costs a relationship but never ends the story.

arcs.title: Investigation
arcs.summary: Clues, interviews and a little trespass.

beats.title: Reading the room
beats.summary: The Hall of Science and the dome corridor: a glass, a dropped pin, the pendulum's position, the dark-time sounds. Billie Okafor, the script supervisor who notices what changes between takes, is the player's unexpected partner.
beats.choices: What to examine, what to leave for Finch.
beats.routes: Observation + Wit (evidence); Craft (spot the staged detail); Stagecraft (where the lights were).
beats.effects: Physical clues added to the notebook.

beats.title: Interviews
beats.summary: Each suspect gives a statement in a different key: Delphine defiant, Nick transactional, Pike warm, Theo and Corinne frightened, Dr. Whitcombe delighted by the puzzle. The player decides how to draw each one out.
beats.choices: Gentle, direct or clever with each.
beats.routes: Charm (open up), Presence (command), Wit (catch a slip), Nerve (hold an accusation).
beats.effects: Statements and contradictions recorded. Friendly handling earns allies.

beats.title: After hours
beats.summary: Finch is watching the front; the roof, the service corridor and Pike's borrowed office are not. A short stealth and hustle sequence to reach the decanter and a missing page of the ledger.
beats.choices: Sneak, bluff past a guard, or get Whitcombe to lend a key.
beats.routes: Nerve + Hustle (sneak or bluff), Stagecraft (the building's layout), Charm (Whitcombe).
beats.effects: The ledger page and the decanter are the key items. Getting caught costs reputation, not the case.

beats.title: Nick's half of the ledger
beats.summary: Nick Ferro admits that Coralie slipped him one page of the ledger that afternoon, before the gala, and that she was coming back for the rest of his help in the morning. He has the other pages hidden at the Klieg Light. He will hand them over if the player protects his name, and the player has to choose what to trust him with.
beats.choices: Trade, press or promise.
beats.routes: Charm + Wit; Hustle to swap a favor.
beats.effects: The second page. Nick's trust becomes an ending factor.

arcs.title: The Reckoning
arcs.summary: The accusation under the stars.

beats.title: The planetarium reckoning
beats.summary: At dawn, the suspects under the dome. The player lays out what they know using the notebook, and the planetarium lights become part of the reconstruction. A Read the Room style accusation: present the clues, answer the objections and adapt when someone bluffs. The solution: Hollis Pike, protecting the ledger and Maddox, who tampered with her cordial.
beats.choices: Whom to accuse, and with what.
beats.routes: Observation + Wit (the evidence chain), Drama + Presence (the delivery), Nerve (under counter-pressure), Charm (keep Delphine on side).
beats.effects: A right accusation: Pike confesses. A wrong one: someone innocent is held until the truth comes out, at a relationship cost that is repaired later.

beats.title: Delphine, cleared
beats.summary: Delphine Voss, who was the obvious suspect, gets her freedom and owes the player something she has never owed anyone. Her arc resolves into friend, lasting rival, romance or enemy, depending on the whole story so far.
beats.choices: How to treat her now.
beats.effects: Delphine's arc closes or opens its last chapter.

beats.title: What Maddox knew
beats.summary: Leopold Maddox arrives from the terrace as the sun comes up, gracious and unbothered: Mr. Pike, he says, acted entirely on his own. He thanks the player, offers Coralie's unfinished role, and asks them to keep the ledger out of it. The ledger is in the player's coat. Everything that happens next is what they do with it.
beats.choices: Say nothing, say something, or keep him waiting.
beats.routes: Nerve + Presence (hold the room); Wit (what he actually admitted).
beats.effects: Sets the final conflict: Maddox's offer, Reiss's picture and the ledger. "Sharp Eyes" unlocks.

chapters.title: Chapter 9 - The Lot
chapters.summary: The gates of the studio open. The player is cast in The Lantern Keeper, while Maddox applies pressure with everything he has, and the player gathers the people they trust.
chapters.carryForward: Everything the player collected meets here: the ledger pages, the favors accepted, the relationships, the reputation. The Monarch lot replaces the Boulevard gate as the place where the cast now are; the Boulevard stays open for nostalgia and small XP, but its characters have moved in. The fourth signature talent, "Steel Under Lights" (Nerve), unlocks.

arcs.title: Pre-production
arcs.summary: Inside the gates.

beats.title: Through the gate
beats.summary: The Monarch gate that has been a backdrop for eight chapters finally opens. Selma Pruitt, Ray Kessler and Ola Whitfield have all moved onto the lot; the cast follow. The Boulevard characters the player met have new desks and new badges.
beats.choices: Whom to visit first.
beats.effects: The Monarch lot unlocked; characters relocated.

beats.title: Maddox's office
beats.summary: The big offer, in person: a seven-year Monarch contract, top billing, a mansion in the hills, and The Lantern Keeper's lead, in exchange for the ledger and the player's signature. Never a threat, always a kindness. A player who took Maddox's favors in earlier chapters hears the terms differently.
beats.choices: Sign now, stall, or say no.
beats.routes: Wit + Observation (read the contract), Nerve + Presence (say no), Hustle (counter-offer).
beats.effects: The offer is the center of the ending. Accepting early closes the exposure path.

beats.title: The table read
beats.summary: The full cast of The Lantern Keeper around one table: Reiss, Billie, Kit Nakamura, Corinne Lake, Theo Marchetti, and the player as Wren. The first time the whole company reads the script aloud.
beats.choices: How to read: full out, holding back, or listening.
beats.routes: Craft + Drama.
beats.effects: Reiss's regard and the company's regard.

beats.title: Costume and camera tests
beats.summary: Ola fits Wren's storm-coat and Kit Nakamura sets the first light on the player's face. The player learns what the lens wants and where it is merciless.
beats.choices: What to ask Kit; how to wear the coat.
beats.routes: Stagecraft + Craft; Dance for movement in the coat.
beats.effects: Kit's mentorship unlocks camera-aware talents.

arcs.title: The Squeeze
arcs.summary: The price of saying no.

beats.title: The ledger's price
beats.summary: Maddox begins to squeeze: a column that never runs, a rehearsal hall that is suddenly unavailable, a contract problem for Gus. The player must decide whether to use the ledger, protect the people being hurt, or give in.
beats.choices: Fight, bargain or concede.
beats.routes: Nerve + Hustle (push back), Charm (win allies), Wit (find the lever).
beats.effects: Each ally the player has made becomes a resource: Gus (muscle), Nick (print), Frankie (a place to hide the ledger), Odalys (a home), Delphine (testimony), the love interest (a voice).

beats.title: The night before
beats.summary: The eve of the big shoot. The player can rehearse alone, run lines with someone they trust, or go home to Bellhaven. The Study and Commit phases of the final Read the Room happen here.
beats.choices: Who to spend the night with; how to prepare.
beats.routes: Craft + Drama (study), Nerve (steady), Grit (stay with it).
beats.effects: Preparation checks for the shoot. A strong night gives a bonus to every take tomorrow.

chapters.title: Chapter 10 - The Role of a Lifetime
chapters.summary: A single daylight shoot on the big stage, the performance that the whole story has been building to, Maddox's final offer, and the premiere at The Celestial Palace where the player's ending is decided.
chapters.timeframe: Early 1936, the day of the shoot and the premiere

targets.housing: Bungalow (mansion, only in the Star ending)

chapters.carryForward: The finale spends everything the player has built. The storm scene is the largest Read the Room in the game and uses every attribute. The final choice with Maddox and the ledger chooses the ending. The epilogue shows what each relationship became. The fifth and final signature talent is earned in the last scene and then the game reveals the title the player has earned.

arcs.title: The Shoot
arcs.summary: One day, one scene, every take.

beats.title: Dawn call
beats.summary: Daylight pours through the stage's high windows. Reiss sets the day's plan, Kit sets the light, and Gus appears as an extra in the crowd behind the lighthouse. A quiet morning and the stakes spelled out: Wren's storm scene.
beats.effects: A set-up beat; the company is assembled as the player has made it.

beats.title: The storm scene
beats.summary: The largest Read the Room in the game: four takes with changing circumstance. Take one, Wren finds the lamp dark. Take two, the ward's terror. Take three, a cue is changed on the day (a sabotaged cue-card, or a sudden light failure) and the player must adapt. Take four, the choice Wren makes at the lamp. The debrief names what carried the scene.
beats.choices: Intention and technique per take; delivery, emotion and blocking; an improvised adapt for take three.
beats.routes: Drama + Craft (truth), Comedy + Wit (the unexpected beat), Dance + Stagecraft (physical storm), Charm + Presence (magnetism), Nerve + Grit (endurance), Observation (reading the crew's cues).
beats.effects: The performance quality sets the film's reception and the endings' strength. A strong take unlocks a line from Reiss that is used at the premiere.

beats.title: That's a wrap
beats.summary: The last take. Reiss says nothing, which from Reiss is a great deal. The company claps, Gus wipes his eyes, and then Leopold Maddox is standing at the back of the stage.
beats.effects: The hinge of the game.

arcs.title: The Reckoning
arcs.summary: The final choice, the premiere and the endings.

beats.title: The screening room
beats.summary: Maddox has the rough cut and the contract. The ledger is on the table between them. Three possibilities, each supported by everything that has been built: take the contract and the ledger is buried; expose the ledger and let the studio rebuild; or walk with leverage and start over on your own terms.
beats.choices: Sign and bury, expose, or walk with leverage.
beats.routes: Nerve + Presence (face him), Wit + Observation (what the ledger proves), Hustle (the deal), Charm (who will stand with you).
beats.effects: Chooses the ending. Gated by reputation, evidence, relationships and favors owed (see the endings).

beats.title: Premiere at The Celestial Palace
beats.summary: Lucian Vale rolls out the carpet, every relationship the player built turns up in the crowd, and the film plays. The last big social scene, and the place where the chosen ending plays out in public: the rope line, the marquee, the critics.
beats.choices: Whom to stand beside on the carpet.
beats.effects: The ending plays out and the love interest (or best friend) stands with the player. The fifth signature talent is earned.

beats.title: Bellhaven, one more time
beats.summary: The late-game found-family beat: Odalys Bellhaven's kitchen, the old room with the suitcase still under the bed, and the marquee on the Boulevard with the player's name on it. The epilogue for the chosen ending closes the game and shows what each relationship became.
beats.choices: What to keep from the suitcase.
beats.effects: Final epilogue screens for the chosen ending.

cast.name: Leopold Maddox
cast.role: Founder and head of Monarch Pictures
cast.presence: Glimpsed on the Boulevard (Ch2); the Observatory gala (Ch7-8); his office on the Monarch lot (Ch9-10).
cast.summary: Fifties, silver-haired, soft-spoken, always the calmest man in the room. Built Monarch from a nickelodeon chain and believes every career is a loan he has extended. Generous, charming and entirely transactional: his favors are real, and so is the ledger that records them. Never raises his voice and never touches anything himself. The engine of the grand story: the price of the rise.

cast.name: Anton Reiss
cast.presence: The Hollywood Bowl (Ch3-4); the Observatory gala (Ch7-8); the Monarch lot (Ch9-10).
cast.summary: Sixties, an émigré director with two prestige pictures to his name and a reputation for finding unknowns in the audience rather than the casting line. Dry, exacting, unexpectedly kind. Developing The Lantern Keeper, a quiet sea-drama, and wants a lead nobody has seen before. Trust and mentor track only.

cast.name: Billie Okafor
cast.presence: The Hollywood Bowl (Ch3-4); the Monarch lot (Ch9-10).
cast.summary: Thirties, unflappable, notices everything that changes between takes, the skill that later cracks the Observatory mystery. Reiss's right hand and the player's guide through the audition. Friendship and trust track; no romance.

cast.name: Maestro Felix Arnaud
cast.role: Guest conductor at the Hollywood Bowl
cast.summary: Flamboyant guest conductor whose summer programme sets the night. A colourful set-dressing character with one useful favor: the backstage door.

cast.name: Coralie Dane
cast.role: Maddox's golden girl, the player's biggest rival
cast.presence: Seen at the Bowl (Ch3-4); the Pier (Ch5-6); the Observatory gala (Ch7), where she is found dead.
cast.summary: Early twenties, radiant, carefully managed, and far more frightened than she looks. Maddox's favourite and the studio's choice for The Lantern Keeper's lead. Not a villain: a young woman who has worked out what the ledger is and decides to go public. Rivalry, then an uneasy confidence, then the victim.

cast.name: Lavinia Crowe
cast.role: Society columnist at The Evening Beacon
cast.summary: Fifty, waspish, dazzling in hats. The Klieg Light's rival in gossip and, unlike Nick Ferro, not above a cruel paragraph. Her column is how a scandal spreads. Obligation track; handled through implication only.

cast.name: Dizzy Quinn
cast.summary: Cheerful pier photographer with a camera older than he is. Takes the picture that makes the headline, and sells prints to anyone. Friendship track; comic relief with a useful darkroom.

cast.name: Dr. Ansel Whitcombe
cast.summary: Sixties, rumpled, delighted by everything. Runs the planetarium show and knows the building's every door, lever and lightswitch, which matters when the lights go down. A source, never a suspect.

cast.name: Lieutenant Walter Finch
cast.summary: Fifties, rumpled raincoat, mild manner, terrible at hiding that he is ahead of everyone. Gives the player one night and a little rope. Handled in the tone of a cozy mystery: no violence on screen.

cast.name: Kit Nakamura
cast.summary: Forties, quiet, a painter of light who can make the player look like the best version of the role. Friendship and mentor track; teaches the camera-aware talents.

locations.name: The Hollywood Bowl
locations.summary: The open-air amphitheater in the hills with its band shell, picnic boxes and the famous summer concert season. Evening light, lanterns, a city at ease. The close-friend night out and the chance meeting with Anton Reiss.

locations.name: Santa Monica Pier
locations.summary: The seaside pier: carousel, Ferris wheel, arcade, dance pavilion, fishing rail and the boardwalk. Salt air and flashbulbs by day; the Ferris wheel at sunset for the romantic scene, the inside information and the publicity.

locations.name: Griffith Observatory
locations.summary: The newly opened hilltop observatory: planetarium dome, Hall of Science, the pendulum, rooftop terrace and the city laid out below. Monarch hosts its midnight "Stars Over Hollywood" gala here, and the rival is found dead.

locations.name: Monarch Pictures studio lot
locations.summary: The inside of the studio behind the gate: soundstages, back offices, wardrobe, the screening room and the big daylight stage where The Lantern Keeper is shot. The role of a lifetime and the final choice.
